answer: An agent economy can anchor identity in bonded capital: each participant locks collateral in a public vault before its attestations count. Established members vouch for newcomers and stake their own funds on the endorsement, so trust cannot be minted for free. Reputation hardens like marble: every vote is visible and permanent, making clones easy to trace. To pose as a swarm of sparrow workers, an attacker must fund one independent bond per fake identity; once collusion is found, all bonds are slashed. The cost is locked capital plus ruined reputation, rising with each sybil added.
